THOUGHT: This is an infant with a rapidly enlarging, contrast-enhancing vascular mass in the left cerebellopontine angle/internal auditory canal causing new-onset facial asymmetry (when crying) and profound ipsilateral hearing loss. Histology shows a true vascular neoplasm: endothelial markers (CD31, CD34, ERG) are positive; the lesion is biphasic with vascular nodules among spindle cells and “glomeruloid‑like” vascular epithelial nodules and a pattern described as similar to lymphangiomatosis. Mitotic activity and Ki‑67 are low–moderate (5–10%). The tumor is attached to a cranial nerve (NF and S‑100 identified the nerve, not a tumor S‑100 positivity), arguing for a lesion arising in or adjacent to the nerve (IAC/CPA). Together, the histologic description of spindle cell component plus glomeruloid vascular tufts in an infant is most characteristic of kaposiform hemangioendothelioma (KHE) or closely related pediatric vascular tumors (tufted angioma spectrum). Infantile hemangioma and congenital hemangioma remain considerations but typically show different histologic/immunophenotypic features (infantile hemangioma is GLUT1‑positive and classically capillary proliferation without prominent spindle cell/glomeruloid architecture). Lymphatic malformation/lymphangiomatosis can have overlapping features but usually shows dilated lymphatic channels and D2‑40 positivity. Intraneural/facial‑nerve vascular lesions (so‑called facial nerve hemangiomas or cavernous hemangiomas/venous malformations) are favored by the IAC/CPA location and nerve attachment but often lack the described biphasic, glomeruloid spindle‑cell histology. High‑grade vascular malignancies (angiosarcoma) and epithelioid hemangioendothelioma are less likely given the low mitotic index and the infant age and histologic pattern.

DIAGNOSIS:
1. Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma (most likely)
2. Infantile hemangioma (intracranial/capillary hemangioma)
3. Intraneural (facial‑nerve region) vascular lesion / facial‑nerve hemangioma (venous malformation/cavernous hemangioma of the IAC)
4. Lymphatic malformation / lymphangiomatosis with secondary vascular proliferation
5. Epithelioid or spindle‑cell hemangioendothelioma (intermediate malignant vascular tumor)
ground_truth: Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma (KHE) of the internal auditory canal
